title: Average Conditional Slope for Gaussian Doses at a Rough Vanishing-Variance Boundary
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound fixed-triple frontier subfield below the field floor; paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4 and salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: only at the single smoothness triple (2,1,1/10), not an all-smoothness frontier.

The package falls short of a higher score because the benchmark is highly specialized, the certified constants are unusably conservative, and no practical or broader theoretical evidence establishes significance beyond this fixed point.
paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a matched n^(-2/5) minimax MSE and n^(-1/5) honest connected-interval length on the fixed Gaussian-dose class, including an independently audited polynomial-kernel lemma. D0.5 found the mathematics sound but graded the single-triple benchmark subfield, below the field novelty floor, with no bounded in-scope route to field. Lean formalization did not begin; follow-on work would need a broader frontier or published-class result, plus the recorded positioning and prose repairs.
tldr: The project fixes the Gaussian-dose boundary experiment at \((\kappa,s,\eta)=(2,1,1/10)\) and proves a same-class match: minimax mean-squared error \(n^{-2/5}\) and uniformly honest connected-interval length \(n^{-1/5}\) for the unweighted average conditional slope. A total observable degree-twelve close-pair score with an independent clipped scale pilot and a deterministic risk radius attains the upper rates. A bounded degree-thirty-one moment-matching law supplies the log-free lower rates. The uniform polynomial-kernel theorem certifies all twelve noncentral moment terms and the integrated common-observation projection bounds, with no certificate term slower than \(n^{-2/5}\).
gap: Published average-derivative inference requires either a positive conditional-variance floor or regular nuisance behavior, and published close-pair methods do not study an integrated causal covariance divided locally by a variance that vanishes as \(x^2\). The closest same-experiment internal result has a logarithmic loss in its rough lower bound and no feasible upper at this point.
fill: A bounded moment-matching mixture gives a log-free same-class converse, while the polynomial close-pair statistic and deterministic radius give observable attainment if the stated uniform kernel audit succeeds. Both decision criteria are evaluated on the identical model class, and the global normalized slope is retained only as a diagnostic comparator.
